messages:
maria: Hey all — first day here! Quick question about API keys. For local dev and playing with the hosted endpoints, should I be using the sandbox key or a hosted key? Also planning to run some streaming tests in CI (GitHub Actions). Any recommendations on which key to store in repo secrets and how to avoid hitting sandbox quotas? Thanks!

devon: welcome! :wave: Use sandbox keys for local/dev experimentation. Hosted keys are for prod/staging. Sandbox has low default quota but supports streaming. For CI e2e tests we usually use a hosted 'test' key scoped to non-billing org or a short-lived token.

samir: if you need more sandbox quota for onboarding, ping @devex with your org and CI job name. They can bump temporarily. There's also an internal form: https://go.redwood.dev/sandbox-requests

elaine: for GitHub Actions we recommend not storing a long-lived hosted key. Use the devex token service via OIDC: in GH Actions you can request a short-lived hosted token with role 'ci-test'. Example in workflow:
```
- name: Get short-lived key
  run: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACTIONS_TOKEN" https://internal.redwood.devex/api/ci-token?role=ci-test -o key
- name: run tests
  env: REDWOOD_API_KEY: $(cat key)
```
If that's not set up for your repo ping @devex.

devon: If you must store a key, create a hosted key with minimal scopes, rotate often, and add IP allowlist to the key if possible. Avoid committing to repo.

devex-bot: Devex: Sandbox quota request submitted by samir on behalf of @maria. Request ID: SR-202603-87. ETA ~2 business days.

maria: thanks! one more: what's the default behavior when you hit sandbox 429s during streaming? backoff or partial responses?

samir: client should exponential backoff on 429. For streaming we fall back to chunked re-tries (dev docs). If you're doing live testing, best to use hosted test key to avoid throttling.

elaine: also note rate limit buckets per-key per-route. Console shows token usage per key under Observability -> Keys.

maria: perfect — pinned. I'll ping devex to enable OIDC for my repo. :thumbsup:
